note: Wording-only rewrites of the frozen audit annotations for scenario_031 head_medicaid_eligible (scripts/apply_rewrites.py applies them; tests/test_annotation_rewrites.py keeps them in force). Each replaces a field's whole old text with its whole new text. None changes a failure_source, failure_subtype, reference_suspect flag, exclusion, reference or score.

rewrites.old: At 67, the head qualifies as aged, so the engine tests Medi-Cal through the optional senior-or-disabled pathway (California's Aged & Disabled FPL program). This is a non-MAGI pathway with a 138% FPL income limit. Countable income is gross income minus health insurance premiums, including the Medicare Part B standard premium (about $202.90/month, or about $2,435/year in 2026). That brings the $23,853 gross down to about $21,400, below 138% FPL (about $21,600). The $4,200 in bank assets easily passes California's asset test. Almost every model compared gross or near-gross income with the limit and never subtracted the Part B premium. Others used the wrong threshold (100% FPL or the SSI rate), applied the $2,000 SSI resource limit, or denied that an aged person has a Medicaid category.
rewrites.new: At 67 the head is aged (65 or older), which alone meets the category condition of the engine's optional senior-or-disabled pathway; it needs no disability or SSI receipt. The adult expansion group (ages 19 to 64, no Medicare eligibility) does not apply, but in the engine's Medicaid rules Medicare eligibility bars only that group. The pathway counts income under SSI rules: Social Security ($9,445.47, in full), the $13,608 pension and the $800 IRA distribution give $23,853.47; the $1,165 of alimony paid is not subtracted. In place of SSI's $20 monthly general income exclusion, the engine applies California's $230 monthly disregard ($2,760 a year), leaving $21,093.47, under the $22,024.80 limit (138% of the 2026 poverty guideline of $15,960). The $4,200 in bank assets is far below California's $130,000 asset limit for the pathway. The engine also models a $2,434.80 Medicare Part B premium for the head, but countable income does not subtract it: with the premium at zero, or the head not enrolled in Medicare, countable income is still $21,093.47. Most models (29 of 43) miscounted income: most of those compared about $23,853 with the limit, a few applied only SSI's $20 exclusion or an exclusion of unstated size, and several asserted without figures that income was too high. The rest used the wrong threshold (100% of the poverty guideline or an SSI income limit), applied SSI's $2,000 resource limit or otherwise judged the $4,200 too much, or missed that age alone gives the head a category.
rewrites.reason: The old note said countable income subtracts health insurance premiums, including the Medicare Part B premium, and compared about $21,400 with a 138% FPL limit of about $21,600 (2025 guideline). The engine applies California's $230 monthly disregard and the 2026 guideline: $21,093.47 against $22,024.80.

rewrites.old: PolicyEngine determined that the head of household is eligible for Medicaid in California as a senior-or-disabled individual. The person, age 67, qualifies through the optional senior-or-disabled category (a non-MAGI pathway) because they meet three conditions: they are aged or disabled (is_ssi_aged_blind_disabled = True), they satisfy the income test under this category (is_optional_senior_or_disabled_income_eligible = True), and they meet the asset limits (is_optional_senior_or_disabled_asset_eligible = True). Additionally, the person satisfies California's immigration status requirements, having been in the United States for 5 years. Under the senior-or-disabled category, countable income is calculated by deducting health insurance premiums, including Medicare Part B, from gross income, which results in the household falling within California's income limits for this eligibility group.

At 67 the head is aged, which meets the category's first condition (is_ssi_aged_blind_disabled = True) without SSI receipt or a disability; the adult expansion group (ages 19 to 64) does not apply, and in the engine's Medicaid rules Medicare eligibility bars only that group. Income follows SSI rules: Social Security ($9,445.47, counted in full), the private pension ($13,608) and the IRA distribution ($800) total $23,853.47; the $1,165 of alimony paid is not subtracted. California's $230 monthly income disregard ($2,760 a year), which takes the place of SSI's $20 general income exclusion, leaves countable income of $21,093.47, within the limit of 138% of the 2026 federal poverty guideline for one person, $22,024.80 (is_optional_senior_or_disabled_income_eligible = True). Countable resources are the $4,200 bank balance, under California's $130,000 limit for an individual (is_optional_senior_or_disabled_asset_eligible = True). The household lists no immigration status, so the engine's default status (citizen) applies and the immigration test passes.
